claims.statement: The repository root Cargo.toml defines a Cargo workspace with exactly two members: `frontend/src-tauri` (the Tauri app crate whose library is named `app_lib` with crate-types staticlib/cdylib/rlib, and whose thin `main.rs` only initializes env_logger and calls `app_lib::run()`) and `llama-helper` (a standalone binary crate wrapping llama-cpp-2 that is never linked into the app).

The Meetily architecture is a Tauri 2.x shell: a static-exported Next.js 14 UI (output: 'export', frontendDist ../out, dev on port 3118) communicates with the Rust core only via `invoke` commands and Tauri events (wrapped by thin service modules in frontend/src/services), while the Rust core owns the audio pipeline, transcription engines, summary generation, and SQLite persistence.

The top-level modules of the compiled app are exactly those declared in lib.rs: analytics, api, audio (with the audio/transcription subtree), config, console_utils, database, notifications, ollama, onboarding, openai, anthropic, groq, openrouter, parakeet_engine, state, summary (with summary_engine), tray, utils, and whisper_engine.

src/audio_v2/ (an unfinished modern-audio rewrite) and src/lib_old_complex.rs (the previous ~2,400-line lib.rs) are not declared as modules in lib.rs and therefore are not compiled into the application binary; they are legacy/dead code.

Four managed states are registered before setup: whisper_engine::parallel_commands::ParallelProcessorState (optional ParallelProcessor plus shared SystemMonitor; worker initialization caps requested workers at 4 and at the resource-safe count), NotificationManagerState (Arc<RwLock<Option<NotificationManager<Wry>>>> populated asynchronously during setup), audio::init_system_audio_state (optional SystemAudioDetector), and summary::summary_engine::ModelManagerState (Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<ModelManager>>>>, lazily initialized on first use if startup init fails).

AppState { db_manager: DatabaseManager } is the shared SQLite handle added during setup or by the onboarding database commands; DatabaseManager wraps a sqlx SqlitePool and commands across api, summary, audio import/retranscription, and onboarding obtain it via state.db_manager.pool().

The lib.rs startup sequence registers plugins first (single-instance — desktop-only, where a second launch just focuses the main window — then notification, store, dialog, updater, and process), then manages state, and in .setup() creates the system tray, spawns notification manager initialization, sets Whisper/Parakeet model directories and spawns whisper_init and parakeet_init in the background, spawns built-in AI ModelManager init with lazy fallback, sets the bundled templates dir to resource_dir()/templates, and blocks on database::setup::initialize_database_on_startup.

database::setup::initialize_database_on_startup is the only blocking init step (run via tauri::async_runtime::block_on inside .setup()). On a normal launch it constructs the DatabaseManager and manages AppState; on first launch (no meeting_minutes.sqlite) it instead emits a delayed first-launch-detected event, and AppState is created later by the onboarding commands import_and_initialize_database or initialize_fresh_database, which also emit database-initialized for the UI.

The main window implements close-to-tray behavior: the on_window_event handler intercepts CloseRequested for the 'main' window, prevents the close, and hides the window so the app keeps running in the tray.

On RunEvent::Exit the app blocks on two cleanup steps: AppState.db_manager.cleanup() which runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) and closes the connection pool (skipped with a warning if AppState is absent on first launch), and summary::summary_engine::force_shutdown_sidecar() which sends the sidecar shutdown command and force-kills after 3 seconds.

SQLite storage lives at app_data_dir/meeting_minutes.sqlite. If only the legacy meeting_minutes.db exists it is copied over and migrated; sqlx::migrate! runs the embedded migrations on every open. If opening fails with a malformed/corrupt error, orphaned -wal/-shm files are deleted and the connection is retried once.

The initial database schema creates meetings, transcripts, summary_processes, transcript_chunks, settings, and transcript_settings tables, all referencing meetings with ON DELETE CASCADE; later migrations add OpenRouter/Gemini keys, licensing, speaker fields, and meeting notes.

llama-helper is a JSON-lines process: it reads generate/ping/shutdown requests from stdin and writes response/pong/goodbye/error lines to stdout, exiting on stdin EOF or after an idle timeout (LLAMA_IDLE_TIMEOUT, default 300 s) that both the helper and the app's SidecarManager honor. It is bundled via tauri.conf.json externalBin binaries/llama-helper, resolved from MEETILY_LLAMA_HELPER, then next to the executable with a target-triple suffix (with a fuzzy llama-helper* match), then RESOURCE_DIR, then dev workspace paths; it is spawned with piped stdio and lowered priority (nice -n 10 on Unix, BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS with no window on Windows), and SidecarManager::ensure_running restarts it when the requested model path changes.

The built-in AI flow is: ModelManager downloads GGUF models (Qwen 3.5 / Gemma 3 catalog) into app_data_dir/models/summary and exposes status via builtin_ai_* commands; generate_with_builtin resolves a cached model path, formats the prompt with the model's chat template, applies sanitized per-model sampling presets, races generation against a CancellationToken (cancellation shuts the sidecar down), while shutdown_sidecar_gracefully drains active requests and force_shutdown_sidecar is reserved for app exit.

ffmpeg is bundled three ways: build.rs calls build/ffmpeg.rs ensure_ffmpeg_binary() which verifies a cached per-target binary in frontend/src-tauri/binaries/ or downloads one from the Zackriya-Solutions/ffmpeg-binaries GitHub release (failing the build otherwise); tauri.conf.json bundles binaries/ffmpeg as externalBin; and audio::ffmpeg::find_ffmpeg_path() resolves it at runtime next to the executable, then PATH, ~/.local/bin (macOS), the working directory, and Tauri resource/lib folders with an ffmpeg-sidecar auto-install fallback — consumed by encode.rs, incremental_saver.rs, and decoder.rs (converting formats Symphonia cannot demux, e.g. mkv/webm/wma, to WAV).

Live recording flow: start_recording* commands validate the configured transcription model (defaulting to Parakeet parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8 when no config exists), then delegate to audio::recording_commands which owns a global RecordingManager; the manager starts AudioStreamManager (raw mic plus optional system streams), AudioPipelineManager (48 kHz adaptive mixing, then Silero VAD which internally resamples to 16 kHz and emits speech segments), and RecordingSaver (incremental audio checkpoints). A single serial worker consumes segments so transcript-update events are emitted in chronological order, and the Rust side also listens to its own transcript-update events to persist transcript history for reload sync.

On stop_recording the pipeline is force-flushed and the app waits for all queued transcription chunks with a 10-minute cap before unloading the configured Whisper or Parakeet model, emitting recording-shutdown-progress stages so the UI can show progress.

Summary generation is asynchronous: api_process_transcript persists the transcript chunk record, spawns SummaryService::process_transcript_background in the background, and returns a process id immediately; the frontend reads progress and results from summary_processes via api_get_summary, and api_save_meeting_summary writes the summary JSON through SummaryProcessesRepository.

Summary templates are JSON files resolved with a fallback strategy: user custom templates from the OS data directory (e.g. ~/Library/Application Support/Meetily/templates/) override bundled templates from resource_dir()/templates (set at startup), which override templates embedded in the binary; tauri.conf.json ships templates/*.json as bundle resources.

Analytics are PostHog-based (posthog-rs) with AnalyticsConfig defaulting to enabled: false; sanitize_analytics_properties strips sensitive keys (meeting titles, file/folder paths, device names, user agent) before events are sent, and all tracking is exposed as opt-out commands registered in lib.rs.

The tray is created during setup with id main-tray, reflects recording state (Stopped/Starting/Recording/Pausing/Paused/Resuming/Stopping), and its handlers drive recording start/stop (emitting recording-stop-complete for frontend post-processing), window focus, settings navigation, update checks, and quit.

Onboarding status (completed flag, current step, model download status) is persisted in the Tauri store as onboarding-status.json; completing onboarding writes the builtin-ai summary model config and the parakeet transcript config to SQLite before marking onboarding complete, and the tray's can-record check treats completed onboarding as a green light.

The api module serves meeting, transcript, profile, model-config, and custom-OpenAI CRUD natively from AppState's SQLite pool; a legacy Python backend URL (http://localhost:5167) remains hardcoded as APP_SERVER_URL for connection-test and licensing helper commands, while the main data commands no longer call it.

Central configuration constants live in config.rs: DEFAULT_WHISPER_MODEL large-v3-turbo, DEFAULT_PARAKEET_MODEL parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8, and the WHISPER_MODEL_CATALOG used by model discovery; GPU acceleration is a compile-time cargo-feature choice on the app crate (metal auto-enabled on macOS, cuda/vulkan/hipblas/openblas/coreml for other platforms) resolved at runtime by WhisperCompiledBackend::current(), with pnpm scripts forwarding these features to tauri build/dev.
